title: Postmillennialism and Daniel's 70th Week (PMT 2013-028)
author: Kenneth L. Gentry Jr.
summary: Part of a series on Daniel 9:24-27 arguing that the seventieth week follows the sixty-ninth without a gap and that the 'cut off' Messiah is Christ crucified within that week.

title: Why a Gap in Daniel's 70 Weeks?
author: Thomas Ice
summary: Pre-Trib Research Center article summarising the dispensational case for an interval between the sixty-ninth and seventieth weeks, with the seventieth week still future.

title: The Temple and Revelation's Date
author: Kenneth L. Gentry Jr.
summary: Argues from the measuring of the temple in Revelation 11:1-2 that the temple was still standing when John wrote, supporting a date before Nero's death in AD 68.

title: The 70 Weeks and 457 B.C.
author: Ángel Manuel Rodríguez (Biblical Research Institute)
summary: Seventh-day Adventist defence of 457 BC (the decree of Artaxerxes in Ezra 7) as the starting point of the seventy weeks, the basis of the historicist 457 BC to AD 34 chronology.

title: Daniel's Seventy Weeks and the New Exodus (Southern Baptist Journal of Theology 14.1)
author: Peter J. Gentry
summary: Reads the seventy weeks as a jubilee-structured prophecy of a new exodus fulfilled in Christ's first coming, with the destruction of the temple as its sequel.

title: Romans 11: Interpretive Options (chart)
author: Kim Riddlebarger
summary: Teaching chart setting out the main Reformed and other readings of 'all Israel' in Romans 11:26 and the scholars associated with each.

title: The Covenant of the Seventieth Week (in The Law and the Prophets, ed. J. H. Skilton)
author: Meredith G. Kline
summary: Influential Reformed essay reading the seventieth week covenantally: Christ confirms the covenant, and the second half of the week stretches symbolically across the church age.
note: Bibliographic details from standard references; not checked online during research.

title: Redating the New Testament
author: John A. T. Robinson
summary: A liberal Anglican scholar's argument that every New Testament book, Revelation included, was written before AD 70.

title: An Introduction to the New Testament (2nd ed.)
author: D. A. Carson and Douglas J. Moo
summary: Standard evangelical introduction. It weighs the patristic and internal evidence and favours a Domitianic date for Revelation, c. AD 95-96.

title: Israel in Prophecy
author: William Hendriksen
summary: Amillennial study arguing that 'all Israel' is the full number of elect Jews gathered through the gospel age, not a future national conversion.

title: Has the Church Replaced Israel? A Theological Evaluation
author: Michael J. Vlach
summary: Dispensational critique of supersessionism, arguing for a future salvation and restoration of national Israel.

title: The Parousia: A Critical Inquiry into the New Testament Doctrine of Our Lord's Second Coming
author: J. Stuart Russell
summary: Victorian Congregationalist study arguing from the New Testament time texts that the Parousia, resurrection and judgment all took place in connection with AD 70. It is a foundational text for full preterism.

title: The Time Is at Hand
author: Jay E. Adams
summary: An amillennial reading of Revelation that dates the book before AD 70 and takes much of it preteristically.

title: The Prophetic Faith of Our Fathers (4 vols.)
author: LeRoy Edwin Froom
summary: Large Adventist survey of the history of prophetic interpretation, documenting historicist exegesis from the early church through the nineteenth century.

title: The Climax of the Covenant: Christ and the Law in Pauline Theology
author: N. T. Wright
summary: Includes Wright's argument that 'all Israel' in Romans 11:26 is the whole people of God, Jew and Gentile, redefined around the Messiah.
